primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Mixed connective tissue disease is a systemic autoimmune overlap syndrome strongly associated with high-titer anti-U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U1-RNP) antibodies. The U1 snRNP is a component of the spliceosome that recognizes the 5′ splice site of pre-mRNA and participates in intron removal during mRNA maturation.
vignette: A 29-year-old woman has recurrent Raynaud phenomenon, persistent puffy fingers, inflammatory polyarthritis, and new symmetric proximal muscle weakness with an elevated creatine kinase concentration. She has no erosions on hand radiographs. Antinuclear antibody testing is strongly positive with a speckled pattern, and serum contains a high titer of anti-U1-RNP antibodies.
lead: The principal autoantigen identified in this patient normally participates in which cellular process?
correct: Recognition of splice sites and removal of introns from precursor messenger RNA
distractors: Initiation of DNA replication at origins by loading the replicative helicase
Charging transfer RNA molecules with their cognate amino acids
Targeting newly synthesized secretory proteins from the cytosol to the rough endoplasmic reticulum
Adding polyubiquitin chains to misfolded cytosolic proteins for proteasomal degradation
distractor_notes: Origin licensing and replicative-helicase loading are DNA-replication functions of origin-recognition/licensing complexes, not U1 snRNP.
Aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases charge tRNA; some are autoimmune targets in inflammatory myopathies, but U1-RNP is a spliceosomal ribonucleoprotein.
Signal-recognition particle directs nascent secretory proteins to the rough ER; it is distinct from U1 snRNP.
Ubiquitin ligases and the proteasome mediate regulated protein degradation, not splice-site recognition.
key_expl: The clinical overlap of Raynaud phenomenon, puffy hands, inflammatory arthritis, and myositis together with high-titer anti-U1-RNP antibodies supports mixed connective tissue disease. U1-RNP is part of the U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein particle in the spliceosome. U1 snRNP recognizes the 5′ splice site of precursor mRNA and helps assemble the spliceosomal complex that removes introns during RNA maturation. This item therefore links the defining serologic marker of MCTD to the normal molecular function of its autoantigen.
objective: Connect mixed connective tissue disease and anti-U1-RNP autoimmunity with the normal role of U1 snRNP in pre-mRNA splicing.
